cards.#1: The Contact Cap is navy with a white interlocking NY, Golf Is A Contact Sport scripted down one side panel and “Played between expectation & reality” down the other. High-density embroidery runs front, sides, rear and under the brim, the last of which only the wearer ever sees. Midiron’s copy gives the brand its line: “Every golfer has two games. The one they imagine and the one they play.” Released in August, sold out since.
cards.#2: The Results Cap is black cotton twill on an unstructured five-panel, with Very good swing. Very bad Result. embroidered across the front in Japanese and then in English. A GAR tag sits on the side, short for Golf Apparel Research, Midiron’s own house descriptor. The product page puts it more gently: “This isn’t a lucky golf cap. It’s for the days when you stripe one down the middle and still walk away with a double.”
cards.#3: Midiron hunted down vintage Titleist caps, sent them to Oxy Customs in Melbourne for reworking and released three — one as a giveaway prize and two for sale, each a one-off. The product page carries the only first-person writing anywhere on the site, lowercase and unsigned: “when i was 10, my grandad gave me a hand me down titleist cap because i didn’t have one to wear when we played golf together. sure, it was nothing special to anyone else, but it meant everything to me.”
cards.#4: The black Tour Spec carries the Midiron star wordmark on the front, a Tour Spec script on the side panel and very little else. The copy is the clearest statement of what the brand is for: “It’s made for the quiet parts of golf — early starts, empty fairways, late finishes. The moments that don’t need witnesses. The ones you do for yourself.” Their photography makes the same argument without saying anything.
cards.#5: Photorealistic tree camo — their term for it, and the one in the URL — sits on an unstructured five-panel. The build is cotton twill with a vintage wash and an adjustable strap back, aimed at wearing in rather than out. Midiron’s copy runs: “No loud logos. No clubhouse energy. Just a cap that does its job quietly, until someone who knows notices.”
cards.#6: Midiron published this one first, in December 2025, and the store started here. It shares the unstructured five-panel build, cotton twill and adjustable strap back with the rest of the caps, in a field camo of flatter olives and browns. That makes it the more wearable of the two camo options if you are not committed to looking like you have come straight from a deer stand.
cards.#7: The Detour is their take on a 1990s polo and the most ambitious thing they make: 300gsm cotton in bold black and cream rugby stripes, cut unisex and boxy. There is chest embroidery, a vintage-washed twill appliqué with raw edges across the back, a custom woven label at the hem and a metal MEMBER bag tag. In their words it “sits right without needing to be tucked. Loose where it should be. Structured where it matters.”
cards.#8: All-over camo print covers mid-weight perforated polyester here, with raised silicone print, embroidery and a big arched MIDIRON across the chest. It photographs best under a flash at night, which is clearly the point: almost every shot Midiron has taken of it is on a floodlit course after dark.
cards.#9: The Big Stick is a padded driver cover in what their copy calls a field camo, with embroidered detailing, a custom flag label and a premium velvet lining. The name is either a driver joke or a Teddy Roosevelt joke and works as both. At A$69 it is the cheapest way into the brand that is not a cap, and the only thing Midiron makes that has nothing to do with clothing.

kickers.1: Caps are the brand and have been since December 2025. Most run cotton twill on an unstructured five-panel with a strap back, and most sign off Golf Apparel Research approved — Midiron approving itself. Three of the six are already gone.
kickers.2: Both polos run a unisex boxy cut rather than a golf fit, which is the thesis: “golf clothing never felt like the rest of our wardrobe. It belonged on the course, but nowhere else.” One is heavyweight cotton, the other perforated polyester.
kickers.3: The non-apparel catalogue is one headcover. That is the shape of a brand which has put out nine things in eight months and restocks almost nothing.
